si4_title.answer: Using normative modeling to assess pharmacological treatment effect on brain state in patients with schizophrenia

dc1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: Cam-CAN (Cambridge Centre for Ageing and Neuroscience) dataset with n=652 healthy controls was used to build the normative model. A single-site dataset from Peking University Sixth Hospital included 37 schizophrenia patients and 44 healthy controls for clinical application of the normative model.
dc1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: Data used in the preparation of this work were obtained from the Cam-CAN repository (available at http://www.mrc-cbu.cam.ac.uk/datasets/camcan/) (Shafto et al. 2014; Taylor et al. 2017) (n=652). The Cam-CAN is a large population-based study of the healthy adult life span... Forty healthy subjects and 42 patients with schizophrenia were enrolled... For the following data analysis, 37 subjects with a mean age of 28.41 yr (SD = 8.41) were included

dc2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: Cam-CAN was used to build sex-specific normative age models for dynamic FC features using 10-fold cross-validation. The single-site Peking University data (37 schizophrenia patients, 44 HCs) was used to apply the normative model to assess pharmacological treatment effects.
dc2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: Based on the large public data set Cam-CAN, we estimated sex-specific normative age models for each dynamic FC feature... To improve the generalizability of the model, we estimated the normative models of healthy individuals from Cam-CAN under 10-fold cross-validation... Individualized deviation profiles of 68 features in SCZ patients (including before and after treatment, bSCZ:34, and aSCZ:34) were derived from sex-specific normative age models
dc2_purpose_of_each_dataset.location: Lin2024.pdf.md: Materials and methods / Normative modeling for dynamic FC features, L101-115

model-1.model-name: sex-specific normative age models for dynamic FC features

dc3_hc_n_of_each_normative_model.detail: The study used 652 healthy controls from Cam-CAN to construct sex-specific normative models via 10-fold cross-validation. In each fold, 9 folds (approximately 587 subjects) were used for training and 1 fold for testing. The models were aggregated into final normative models.
dc3_hc_n_of_each_normative_model.supporting_text: Data used in the preparation of this work were obtained from the Cam-CAN repository... (n=652)... we estimated the normative models of healthy individuals from Cam-CAN under 10-fold cross-validation. Specifically, the data were randomly divided into 10 folds. Nine-folds were utilized for building the model, whereas the remaining fold was employed to evaluate the general performance of the model.

dc4_age_info_of_each_normative_model.detail: Age information for the Cam-CAN dataset was provided in Supplementary Table S1. Mean age was 54.9 years with SD of 18.6 years. The exact age range (min/max) was not explicitly reported in the paper, but Cam-CAN is described as a large population-based study of the healthy adult life span.

dc5_sex_info_of_each_normative_model.detail: Sex distribution for the Cam-CAN dataset (n=652) was 322 males and 330 females as reported in Supplementary Table S1. Sex-specific normative models were built separately for females and males. Exact train-phase breakdown per fold is not reported.
dc5_sex_info_of_each_normative_model.supporting_text: Sex (M/F) 322/330... To avoid the potential sex effects on model construction, we separately estimated the normative model in female/male groups.
